title: trouble-tickets-location-is-liveness
owner: CC owns the mechanism. Akien owns the design choice of whether cleared troubles go to the 30-day artifact archive or a longer-lived quiet store.
intention: Trouble tickets adopt location-as-liveness (live in CairnCommons/troubles/, cleared move to artifact archive) and a unified workflow model shared with development tickets (same schema, same inspector, same gate, same field names).
why: CC checked the wrong field (cleared instead of standing) when compiling the inbox — two separate state models meant guessing which vocabulary applied. Location-as-liveness dissolves the guess: a trouble file present in CairnCommons/troubles/ is live; its absence means cleared. No field to misread.
traces_to: Law 4 — a rule that matters is enforced by physics; location-as-liveness makes 'is this trouble live?' a directory listing rather than a field to interpret correctly.
Law 7 — errors are loud and permanent in records of truth; the cleared trouble is kept (git history + archive), never destroyed, but is no longer on the live surface.
Law 1 — a unified workflow model means CC does not re-derive which vocabulary applies to each ticket type.

falsifier.proves_green: code-seam invariant: proved + feeds-back-on-failure. PROVE GATE: clearing moves the file and live() returns only directory contents; a cleared trouble is absent from CairnCommons/troubles/ and present in the archive; a live trouble is present in CairnCommons/troubles/. FEEDS BACK: a red names which invariant broke.
falsifier.proves_red: DONE when (1) clearing a trouble moves the file out of CairnCommons/troubles/ into the artifact archive, and live() is a directory listing with no field checks, and (2) trouble tickets carry the same state/workflow fields as development tickets and the same inspector can read both. WRONG INTENT if git history is lost, if the unified model forces inapplicable fields, or if the archive loses identity.
falsifier.horizon: Moderate — touches the trouble device's clear() method, the live() filter, and adds archive-on-clear logic plus unified schema fields.

questions.a: LOCATION IS LIVENESS: a file in CairnCommons/troubles/ is live; its absence means cleared. No field, no vocabulary, no guess.

GIT HISTORY IS THE PERMANENT RECORD: the move across roots (CairnCommons → ~/.cairn) means the file leaves git. But git keeps the file's last committed state in CairnCommons/troubles/ forever. The archive is operational visibility; git is the record of truth.

SAME SCHEMA, NOT NECESSARILY SAME PATH: Akien said 'same inspector, same gate, same field names' — the interface is unified. Whether the workflow PATH is shared (code-seam@v2) or trouble-specific (OPEN→CLEARED) is a design question for the chart chain.

how.location_as_liveness: On clear, the trouble file moves from CairnCommons/troubles/ to ~/.cairn/logs/cairn/0/artifact_archive/trouble_tickets/ and ages out on the 30-day cycle. The live() filter becomes a directory listing — if the file is in CairnCommons/troubles/, it is live. The git history of the file's last committed state in CairnCommons/troubles/ is the permanent record.
how.unified_model: Trouble tickets adopt the same state/workflow fields as development tickets — state with cursor notation, node_class, schema_version. Whether this means trouble tickets literally use code-seam@v2 or a new trouble node class with a simpler path (OPEN→CLEARED) is a chart-chain question. Akien said 'same schema, same inspector, same gate, same field names' — the interface is shared; the path may differ.
how.archive_mechanism: The archive path needs a cleanup mechanism for the 30-day cycle. Whether this reuses an existing artifact archive cleanup or needs a new one is a survey question.

live() calls fold_pending() and returns _listing(self._root): every *.json at the top, no field read. all() calls fold_pending() and returns _listing(top) + _listing(top/'cleared'). _listing(folder) is the old all() parsing body and returns [] for a missing folder. _read(ident) reads the top file, else cleared/<ident>.json; _cleared_path(ident) names the latter; _drop(path, why) removes an existing file through the artifact door's remove; _write gains where=None (default the top path) and makes where's parent. clear(): on a full clear set standing CLEARED and resolution as today, setdefault node_class and schema_version, set workflow_and_state to WORKFLOW_CLEARED, write the ticket to cleared/<id>.json, then _drop the top file, both with why 'cleared by <by>: <what_changed>'. A partial clear (outstanding parts left) writes in place at the top. amend() writes to the top path if it exists, else to cleared/<id>.json, so an amendment never moves a ticket. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09

raise_trouble(): a file at the TOP (whatever its standing) increments count (count or 0, +1), setdefaults node_class and schema_version and sets WORKFLOW_OPEN. Otherwise a new ticket is written at the top with node_class, schema_version, workflow_and_state WORKFLOW_OPEN, cleared_by copied from the prior ticket (empty when none) and prior_attempts as today; when a prior ticket existed (it was in cleared/), _drop its cleared/ copy with why '<id> recurred after a clear'.
